title: Arkansas State fires coach Butch Jones in sixth season: Source
content:
Arkansas State has fired head coach Butch Jones with two games remaining in the regular season, according to a source briefed on the decision. The person spoke on condition of anonymity Monday night because the move had not been made public.

The Red Wolves are 4-6 this season and could still reach a bowl game, but the school has moved on from Jones, who went 30-43 in six seasons and was coming off bowl appearances each of the last three years. Arkansas State went 2-1 in the bowl games.

Expectations are higher for a program that won at least a share of five Sun Belt championships from 2011-16 across four different head coaches (Hugh Freeze, Gus Malzahn, Bryan Harsin and Blake Anderson). Jones went 2-10 in his first season in 2021, but improved each year to 3-9, 6-7 and then 8-5 in 2024, as one of the youngest rosters in the country grew more experienced.

But the Red Wolves plateaued, going 7-6 last season, and the 2026 season has been a disappointment, with the last four losses coming by a total of 19 points. That included defeats in the last two weeks to Sun Belt bottom-feeder UL Monroe and a struggling Coastal Carolina team.

Jones was previously the head coach at Tennessee (2013-17), Cincinnati (2010-12) and Central Michigan (2007-09).
